transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi. I suppose I came in because... I don't know, I’ve just been taking on far more projects and workshops than I can realistically manage right now. I decided to do all these studio improvements, too. Actually, speaking of the studio, I was just at the lumber yard yesterday looking at these gorgeous reclaimed wood panels for the east wall. The guy working there—I think his name was Jerry—was telling me all about how they source the wood from old barns in upstate New York, which is funny because my aunt used to own a farm up near Syracuse. We used to visit every summer when I was a kid and pick apples. They had this huge golden retriever that would chase the tractor... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. The studio. I've got the improvements, and I'm fielding all these new client calls, and suddenly all the project deadlines and my mortgage are really starting to close in on me. I just... I have no idea how I'm going to get it all done.
Do you often feel overwhelmed or anxious when thinking about all the projects and responsibilities you have?

Well, overwhelmed... yes, I suppose. I mean, it's just so much all at once. The anxiety really creeps up on me mostly at night. Like last night, I was lying in bed thinking about the reclaimed wood for the studio, and then I remembered that I need to buy a new saw blade because my old one is getting dull. I bought it at this little hardware store downtown—they have the best selection of tools, and the owner, Mr. Henderson, he always gives me a discount because I've been going there for years. He actually used to be a carpenter himself before he opened the shop. He made this beautiful rocking chair for his granddaughter, he showed me a picture of it once... 

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, the projects. Yes, it's just... I look at the calendar and see all these deadlines overlapping, and then I think about the mortgage, and it just feels like this giant weight pressing down on my chest. I don't know how I'm going to finish everything.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one thought to another like you did just now?

Well, yes, I suppose I do that quite a bit lately. It's like my brain just won't stay put. I'll sit down in the studio to finish a plate for a contract—something I really need to get done—and then, I don't know, a bird will land at the window. We get these beautiful blue jays this time of year, and they always remind me of the ones my grandmother used to feed when I was little. She had this ornate bird feeder that my grandfather built for her out of cedar. It smelled so wonderful, especially after it rained... 

Wait, what was I saying? Right, the distractions. So I'll be working, and then it's the bird, or I'll glance at a hardware catalog on my desk, or I'll just get this half-formed idea for a completely new workshop, and suddenly I'm pulled completely off course. I just can't seem to stay on one track.
Do you often find yourself preoccupied with your thoughts, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

Well, preoccupied... I guess you could say that. It's more like the thoughts just sort of hijack me. I'll be trying to focus on, say, mixing a specific glaze—I've been trying to perfect this deep cobalt blue, which is incredibly tricky because the copper carbonate has to be measured just right. If you use even a fraction of a gram too much, it turns this murky green in the kiln. My friend Sarah, who runs a pottery co-op downtown, had an entire batch of mugs ruined last month because her assistant misread the scale. She was so upset because they were for this big local artisan market, and those markets are so competitive to get into these days... 

But, um, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, being preoccupied. I don't know, I just... I try to focus, but the thoughts are just so loud, and I end up miles away from what I was actually trying to do.
Have you been engaging in more physical activity than usual lately?

Well, yes, I suppose I have been moving around a lot more. It's like I wake up with this... this humming current inside me right from the morning. Sitting quietly just feels almost impossible lately. So I've been constantly on my feet—rearranging the entire studio, drafting new grant proposals, emailing people I haven't spoken to in months, fussing with all my supplies... 

Speaking of supplies, I found this incredible new supplier for raw clay online. They're based out of Ohio, and they harvest this specific type of stoneware clay that fires to the most beautiful, warm toasted color. I ordered three hundred pounds of it last week because the shipping was discounted if you bought in bulk. The delivery driver was not happy with me when he had to haul it all up to the porch. He was this young kid, probably no older than my nephew David. David just started college, actually, studying environmental science, which I think is just wonderful given how much trouble the climate is in... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost the thread again. What was the question? Oh, physical activity. Yes, I just can't seem to stop moving. If I sit down, that humming feeling just gets louder, so I just keep finding things to do, over and over.
Do you often feel guilty about things that you've done or haven't done?

Guilty? No, not really. I mean, I don't think I have anything to feel guilty about, do I? I've been so productive, getting all these things done. Actually, I was just telling my sister that I feel like I'm finally catching up on years of missed opportunities. She called me yesterday from Seattle. It rains so much there, I don't know how she stands it. I need the sun for my work, the natural light is just essential for seeing the true color of the glazes. If you mix them under fluorescent lights, they look completely different once they're fired. I learned that the hard way back in grad school... 

Oh, what was I saying? Right, guilt. No, I haven't really been feeling guilty. Just busy. Very, very busy.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain thoughts, places, or activities?

Avoiding things? No, I don't think so. I mean, why would I avoid anything right now when everything is just... clicking into place? I've been going everywhere, doing everything. In fact, I went down to the old industrial district yesterday because I heard they were tearing down this beautiful brick warehouse from the 1920s. I wanted to see if I could salvage some of the old ironwork before the demolition crews ruined it. The way they just tear down history in this city is a tragedy, really. 

My grandfather used to work in a factory just like that one, making textiles. He had these huge, calloused hands, but he could weave the most delicate lace. He brought my grandmother a piece of lace from the factory on the day he proposed. They met at a dance hall, which is funny because neither of them were very good dancers. My grandmother always said she stepped on his toes so many times she was surprised he didn't walk with a limp...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Avoiding things? No, no, I haven't been avoiding anything. If anything, I'm trying to fit more into my day, not less.
Do you often worry about things in your daily life?

Worry? No, I wouldn't say I'm worried. I mean, what is there to worry about when I have so much energy to get things done? I'm actually feeling quite the opposite of worried—I feel so capable right now. Like I can finally tackle all those projects I've been putting off. 

Speaking of projects, I started repainting the entire kitchen yesterday. I decided the old yellow just wasn't inspiring enough, so I'm doing this vibrant, deep teal. It reminds me of the ocean in Maine. We used to go to Maine every summer when I was a kid. My dad would rent this little cabin right on the rocky coast, and we'd spend hours looking for sea glass. You know, it takes years for the ocean to tumble those sharp pieces of broken glass into something smooth and beautiful. It's fascinating how nature does that. My brother actually found a perfectly round piece of blue sea glass once, which is incredibly rare. He kept it in a little jar on his desk for years, until his cat knocked it over and it shattered...

Oh, goodness, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Tangents. You asked if I worry. No, honestly, I haven't been worrying about much of anything lately. I'm just too focused on moving forward.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Sleep? Oh, well, I guess I haven't been sleeping as much, but I wouldn't say I *need* less sleep, exactly. I just have so much to do! I've been getting up at, like, 3 or 4 in the morning because my mind is just racing with ideas for the new sculpture series. It's going to be all metal and wire, really industrial. 

I actually went to the hardware store at 6 AM the other day as soon as they opened. The guy working the register, Dave, he's been there for thirty years. He was telling me about how the neighborhood has changed since the 90s. Back then, they used to have this incredible bakery right next door that made the best sourdough. I've tried making sourdough myself, you know, during the pandemic when everyone was doing it. Cultivating the starter is so tricky, though. You have to feed it every day, almost like a pet. I named mine 'Seymour' after that plant in Little Shop of Horrors because it just kept growing and growing... I ended up with so much extra starter I was giving it away to all my neighbors. Mrs. Higgins next door made the most amazing pancakes with hers...

Sorry, what was the question? Sleep? Yeah, I'm probably getting maybe three hours a night right now, but I feel completely fine. Never better, really!
Are you having any difficulties getting along with friends, family, or coworkers because of your recent behavior or energy levels?

Difficulties? Well, maybe a little. I mean, most days lately I've just felt so unusually buoyant, you know? Completely lit up. Like everything in the studio and even out in the garden is finally just clicking perfectly into place. I've been getting so much done. 

But, I suppose... well, my sister was over on Tuesday. She started asking all these questions about my invoices and whether I was keeping track of my commissions, and I just snapped at her. Sharply. I really didn't mean to, but it's like, why are you dragging me down with paperwork when I'm in the middle of a creative breakthrough? She always does that, though. Even when we were kids, she was the practical one. She used to organize her Halloween candy by color and size, and she'd make it last until Easter. I'd eat all mine in three days and then try to trade her my toys for her chocolate. She never went for it. She ended up becoming an accountant, which makes perfect sense. Her husband is an actuary. Can you imagine the dinner conversations? They have this golden retriever named Barnaby who is just the sweetest thing, though. He loves to chase the hose when I water the garden...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, getting along with people. Yeah, I guess I've been a bit irritable if people question my plans or interrupt me. But overall, I just feel so elevated!
Do you feel like you're unusually happy or optimistic most of the time lately?

Happy? Optimistic? Oh, absolutely. Like I was just saying, most days lately I've felt unusually buoyant. Just completely lit up from the inside out. It's like everything in the studio and out in the garden is finally clicking into place, you know? I'm seeing connections between the metalwork and the organic shapes of the hydrangeas that I never noticed before. 

Hydrangeas are so temperamental, though. You have to get the soil acidity just right if you want those deep, vibrant blues. My grandmother used to bury rusty nails around the roots of hers to change the color. She swore by it. She had this massive garden in Savannah, full of Spanish moss and these giant oak trees. We'd sit on the porch drinking sweet tea—real Southern sweet tea, the kind that's practically syrup—and listen to the cicadas. They get so loud down there in the summer, it's almost deafening, but it's a comforting sound, you know? It reminds me of being a kid and having absolutely no responsibilities. Not like now, with all the gallery deadlines and the taxes...

Which reminds me of what I mentioned earlier about my sister. I do get a bit... well, I can snap sharply at anyone who questions my plans or asks about things like invoices right now. It just feels like they're trying to throw a wet blanket over this amazing fire I've got going. But underneath that irritation, yes, I'm just incredibly optimistic. Everything is just so bright.
Do you ever have days where you don't feel as happy or energetic as you've been feeling lately?

Not as happy or energetic? Honestly, no, I haven't really noticed any days like that. I can't even imagine slowing down right now. Slowing down just sounds... boring. It's like when you're driving and you suddenly hit a massive wall of traffic. 

I was driving out to the coast a while back to look for driftwood—I love incorporating natural, weathered textures with the industrial metal I've been using, it creates this beautiful visual tension—and the traffic near the suspension bridge was just at a dead stop. But sitting there, I got to really look at the bridge cables. The geometry of it is absolutely fascinating. It actually inspired me to special-order this specific gauge of copper wire from a distributor in Germany. The shipping was a total nightmare, though. I had to use a translation app just to email their customer service team. My grandfather actually spoke fluent German, but he never taught us. He was a watchmaker, a very precise, very quiet man. He had this incredible collection of antique pocket watches in his study that chimed at all different times, so his house always sounded like a tiny, metallic orchestra... 

Anyway, sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling less energetic. Yeah, no, I haven't had any slow days at all. Just full speed ahead!
Have you been feeling rested and alert on less sleep than you normally need?

Sleep? Oh, well, honestly, I haven't really been sleeping much at all. I mean, why sleep when there's so much to do? I usually just need a couple of hours, maybe three, and then I'm wide awake, completely alert and ready to go. It's like my brain just doesn't need to shut down anymore. 

Which is great, because I've been working on this massive sculpture for the courtyard. It's going to be this huge, kinetic piece that catches the wind. I was out there at 3:00 AM yesterday, measuring the wind currents. You know, the wind at that hour is so different. It's colder, sharper. It reminds me of this trip I took to Iceland years ago. The wind there practically howls. We stayed in this tiny little cabin near a glacier, and the Northern Lights were just... indescribable. Like neon green ribbons dancing across the sky. I tried to paint them when I got back, but you can't really capture that kind of luminescence with just acrylics. You need something that actually emits light. I've been thinking about incorporating LED strips into my metalwork for that exact reason. I found this supplier online that makes these ultra-thin, flexible strips that you can program to pulse to music...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about sleep? Yes, I feel completely rested. Barely sleeping, but totally energized.
Do you ever experience periods where your mood is not as elevated as it has been lately?

Not as elevated? Like, feeling down? No, I really haven't. Honestly, I haven't had a down day in... I don't even know how long. Everything is just moving so fast and feeling so incredible right now. 

It actually reminds me of this time in grad school when we had to put together our final thesis exhibition. Everyone else was stressing out, completely miserable, but I was just on fire. I stayed up for days, welding these huge steel armatures. The sparks from the welder are so mesmerizing, you know? They look like tiny, dying stars just raining down on the concrete floor. My professor at the time, this brilliant guy named Julian, he used to wear these ridiculous thick rubber boots in the studio because he was terrified of getting electrocuted. He told us this story once about how he got shocked fixing a toaster when he was seven, and it completely changed the trajectory of his life. He decided right then and there he was going to make art that felt dangerous. He actually built this installation out of exposed wires and salt water—it was totally against fire code, the university made him take it down after two days. But the smell of the ozone it created... it was like standing in the middle of a thunderstorm. I've always loved thunderstorms. The way the air pressure drops right before the rain starts...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Mood. No, I haven't been feeling low or anything. Just really, really good.
Do you ever have moments where you feel your happiness or energy levels drop, even if it's just for a brief period?

Drop? No, not really. I mean, maybe for a split second if I run out of materials or something, but no, not a real drop. I'm just buzzing all the time. 

It's funny you mention dropping, though, because I was just thinking about gravity the other day. I was watching this documentary about black holes—did you know that time actually slows down the closer you get to one? It's called time dilation. It absolutely blew my mind. I started thinking about how I could represent that in a physical space. Like, creating a room where the visual markers of time—clocks, metronomes, even the lighting—are all slightly out of sync. I actually started sketching it out on these giant rolls of butcher paper. I had to move all the furniture out of my living room just to unroll it. My cat, Barnaby, he was not happy about that. He hates when I rearrange things. He’s a Maine Coon, massive, like a small lion, and he just sat on the edge of the paper glaring at me. I got him from this rescue shelter that was run out of this woman’s basement. She had, like, forty cats down there. It smelled exactly like you'd think it would, but she was so sweet. She gave me this huge bag of catnip that she grew herself in her garden...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, no, my energy hasn't dropped. Not at all. I'm still just flying high.
